dimensions.summary: Canonical truth, dependency direction, dual scope and non-hybrid extraction decisions are locked.
Provider, ontology, backend, consumer and optional native extension boundaries are defined before implementation.
Reference-runtime, bounded-worker and measured native acceleration rules are locked without premature engine claims.
Untrusted inputs, provider isolation, resource bounds and fail-closed admission are design requirements.
Portable locators, redaction and no internal documentation publication are locked.
TypeScript is the reference runtime and native acceleration remains optional and cross-platform gated.
Graph has its own package boundary and the CLI bridge remains prohibited.
Canonical serialization, proof-carrying truth and full versus incremental equivalence are locked as future gates.
Versioned contracts, architecture epochs and staged CLI replacement are required.
Cancellation, partial results, atomic publication and recoverable adapters are explicit design constraints.
Layering, traceability, stage gates and ADR ownership are established.
The package is development-only, allowlisted and independently guarded against publication.

checks.evidence: Local Graph package checks pass at the accepted G0 boundary.
Package quality, boundary, mirror and packed-install guards pass.
The canonical documentation set and accepted ADRs are content-addressed without publishing internal documents or local paths.

remainingRisks: G1 contract wire schemas and semantic fixture corpus are not yet complete.
Rust/native acceleration remains prohibited until G2 reference semantics and G6 measured bottlenecks exist.

approval.rule: Explicit maintainer acceptance of the G0 architecture decisions authorizes G1 contract and conformance work only.
